title: Application, Transfer and Cancellation Terms of the Security Deposits Tiers
content:
How a Security Deposits record can end, other than by a good-payment refund, depends on these tier terms: whether a held deposit is applied to the final bill, whether it is released into a PrePay Power enrollment, whether it may follow the member to a new service account, how quickly payments on a cancelled assessment are refunded, and the order in which a deposit is credited against a final bill.

| Tier | Applied to the final bill | Released into a PrePay Power enrollment | May follow the member to a new service account | Calendar days to refund payments on a cancelled assessment by check | Order of credit on the final bill |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Residential Standard Deposit | yes | yes | yes | 10 | oldest charges first |
| Residential Credit Reestablishment Deposit | yes | yes | yes | 10 | oldest charges first |
| Seasonal Residence Deposit | yes | yes | no | 10 | oldest charges first |
| Farm Service Deposit | yes | yes | yes | 10 | oldest charges first |
| General Service Deposit | yes | yes | no | 10 | oldest charges first |
| Irrigation and Large Power Deposit | yes | no | no | 10 | oldest charges first |

## Reading the table

- A transfer to a new location is open only on the Residential Standard Deposit, the Residential Credit Reestablishment Deposit and the Farm Service Deposit.
- The Irrigation and Large Power Deposit is never released into a PrePay Power enrollment.
- Oldest charges first means the final bill's charges are credited in the order they were billed, the earliest first.
